newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Acacia says no bid plans for Helix.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Acacia says no bid plans for Helix.

text.p: Acacia Resources Ltd managing director Michael Folie said on Friday that his company had no intention at this stage of bidding for Gawler Craton explorer Helix Resources, describing its newly-acquired 17.4 percent holding as a strategic stake.
"We have no intention at this stage of doing anything like that (launching a takeover bid)," Folie told Reuters. "That is quite a different move," he said.
Acacia said earlier on Friday it had bought 17.4 percent of the South Australian explorer, to become the largest single investor. Folie said Acacia paid an average of A$4.20 per share.
Folie said he did not believe Acacia had paid too much for Helix, a sentiment which dominated early morning trade in Acacia. He said the shares were bought over a period of time.
Diamond miner Ashton Mining Ltd said on Thursday it had sold its 12.89 percent stake in Helix, with brokers saying this parcel was traded on-market at an average price of A$4.45 per share.
The Gawler Craton region is regarded as highly prospective and has been the subject of intense exploration and share market scrutiny in the last year.
Acacia, which produces about 350,000 ounces a year from gold mines in Western Australia and the Northern Territory, said the region had the potential to hold world-class gold deposits.
Acacia shares were 13 cents lower at A$2.26 at 11.50 a.m. (0050 GMT), while Helix shares were 10 cents higher at A$4.80, giving it a market capitalisation of A$226.75 million.
